name: Rajma Chawal
subtitle: soft kidney beans in a thick onion-tomato gravy, eaten over plain rice

image.alt: Rajma with jeera rice, saag and raita on a steel thali

ingredients.note: the small dark Jammu variety if you can find it
or a squeeze of lemon at the end

ingredients.qty: 4 cups for the beans, 3 cups for the rice

prepNotes: Soak the rajma in cold water overnight, 8 to 10 hours. Beans soaked for less time stay chalky in the middle no matter how long you cook them.
Rinse the basmati until the water runs clear, then soak it 20 minutes and drain.
Discard the bean soaking water and cook in fresh water — it makes the dish easier on the stomach.

steps.text: Pressure cook the drained rajma with 4 cups fresh water, the bay leaf and 1 tsp salt for 20 minutes at full pressure, then let the pressure fall naturally.
steps.tip: A cooked bean should squash to a paste between finger and thumb with no resistance.

steps.text: While it cooks, heat the oil in a heavy pan and crackle the cumin seeds for 20 seconds.
Add the onion and fry on medium-high, stirring often, until evenly deep brown — a full 12 to 14 minutes.
steps.tip: Pale onions give a thin, pink gravy. Take it to the colour of strong tea.

steps.text: Stir in the ginger, garlic and green chillies and fry 2 minutes until the sharpness goes.
Add the turmeric, coriander powder and chilli powder, stir for 20 seconds, then pour in the tomato puree.
steps.tip: Adding the tomato quickly stops the ground spices burning in the dry pan.

steps.text: Cook the masala down for 10 to 12 minutes until it darkens and oil separates at the sides.
Scoop out a ladle of cooked beans, mash them to a paste, and stir that back in with the rest of the beans and their liquid.
steps.tip: The mashed beans are what makes the gravy cling to rice instead of running off it.

steps.text: Simmer uncovered 20 minutes until the gravy is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. Add hot water if it tightens too far.
Meanwhile boil the rice in 3 cups water with 1/2 tsp salt, covered, on the lowest heat for 11 minutes, then rest 5 minutes off the heat and fork through.
Finish the rajma with garam masala and amchur, taste for salt, and scatter over the coriander.
Serve the rajma ladled over the hot rice.

storage: The rajma keeps 4 days refrigerated and improves overnight; reheat with a splash of water. Cook rice fresh — it goes hard in the fridge. The gravy freezes well for 2 months.
